== Problem ==
'''pdxparse''' emits inline icons as <code><nowiki>{{icon|<code>}}</nowiki></code>
— a positional ''icon code'' that the template maps to a file name, e.g.
<code><nowiki>{{icon|time}}</nowiki></code>, <code><nowiki>{{icon|opinion}}</nowiki></code>,
<code><nowiki>{{icon|political power}}</nowiki></code>. There are roughly 280
such call sites across the parser, so this is the single most load-bearing
template in the output.

Old World Blues and Equestria at War both carry the Paradox-wiki style
<code>Icon</code> and need no change.

The Nation of Nations wiki's <code>Template:Icon</code> is a different template
with the same name. It renders:

<pre>
[[File:{{{iconfile}}}|22px]]
</pre>

It takes a ''named'' <code>iconfile</code> parameter and ignores positional
input, so every <code><nowiki>{{icon|time}}</nowiki></code> in pdxparse output
expands to <code><nowiki>[[File:|22px]]</nowiki></code> and renders as nothing
or as a broken file link.

== Fix ==
Do '''not''' replace the existing template — existing pages call it with
<code>iconfile=</code> and would break. Instead make it accept both forms, by
falling through to a code lookup only when <code>iconfile</code> is absent:

<pre>
&lt;includeonly&gt;{{#if:{{{iconfile|}}}
 | [[File:{{{iconfile}}}|{{{width|22px}}}|link=]]
 | {{#switch: {{lc:{{{1|}}}}}
   | time              = [[File:Time.png|{{{width|22px}}}|link=]]
   | political power   = [[File:Political power.png|{{{width|22px}}}|link=]]
   | opinion           = [[File:Opinion.png|{{{width|22px}}}|link=]]
   | war               = [[File:War.png|{{{width|22px}}}|link=]]
   | exclusivem        = [[File:Mutually exclusive.png|{{{width|22px}}}|link=]]
   | manpower          = [[File:Manpower.png|{{{width|22px}}}|link=]]
   | stability         = [[File:Stability.png|{{{width|22px}}}|link=]]
   | war support       = [[File:War support.png|{{{width|22px}}}|link=]]
   | #default          = &lt;span class="pdx-icon-missing"&gt;&lt;/span&gt;
   }}
 }}{{#if:{{{2|}}}|&amp;nbsp;{{{2}}}}}&lt;/includeonly&gt;
</pre>

=== Why <code>#default</code> is empty ===
An unrecognised code renders nothing visible rather than a red link or a broken
image. Add <code>[[Category:Pages with unrecognised icon codes]]</code> to the
<code>#default</code> branch while you are filling the switch out, then remove
it once the tracking category is empty — that turns the gap into a worklist
instead of scattered breakage.

=== Extending the switch ===
Every icon code pdxparse can emit is a string literal in the parser source. To
list them all:

<pre>
grep -rhoP '\{\{icon\|[^}|]+' src/ | sed 's/{{icon|//' | sort -u
</pre>

Add a row per code that the wiki has a file for; leave the rest to
<code>#default</code>.
